learning_outcomes.text: The elaboration of industrial products requires the use of non-destructive testing methods to detect possible defects. These techniques are also used for monitoring in-service structures (bridges, offshore platforms, aircraft...) to prevent potential failure.
The teaching of these techniques, with the capabilities and limits of each, aims to enable an engineer to choose the most appropriate one and to know how to exploit it optimally.
Among other analytical techniques used in industry, the X-ray diffraction technique, which allows, for example, to calculate residual stresses, will be detailed.

Finally, optical and electron microscopy techniques (destructive techniques, unlike NDT) used both to characterize the microstructure of materials and to analyze fracture surfaces will be presented and illustrated.
X-ray tomography is also a new non-destructive testing technique used to analyze materials.
It will be a question of optimizing these techniques by mastering the physics and mathematical reconstruction techniques. Demonstrations and applications on composite materials will also be proposed.

syllabus_topics: Microscopy and structural and chemical analysis techniques in materials science
degree: Diplôme d'ingénieur Centrale Nantes, spécialité Mécanique (apprentissage)
